basics.name: Alexander Slavschik
basics.label: Senior Frontend Engineer · Game Developer
basics.summary: As a software engineer, I specialize in web and game development. My passion and dedication to programming are not limited to any specific language. I am constantly searching for ways to enhance efficiency and performance in my work. Learning and growing are important to me, and I am eager to make meaningful contributions to my clients' success.

work.name: Evolution
work.summary: Building real-money live casino and game-show titles for a global iGaming platform. Took multiple game clients **from empty repository to production** and maintained a portfolio of live titles played by users worldwide.
highlights: **Built new game clients end-to-end** — project scaffolding, MobX stores, WebSocket transport and message handlers, betting grid, drag-and-drop chips, flying-chip animations, statistics and help screens.
**Engineered complex interactive betting UX**: drag-and-drop chip placement with distance/scaling math, bet and table-limit validation, real-time bet statistics and winner lists.
Delivered responsive, multi-orientation layouts across desktop, tablet and mobile.
Integrated __Rive real-time animations__ behind feature flags and built audio / voice-over systems with regulatory variants.
Implemented regulatory and compliance features and operator-specific branding for multiple game skins.
Drove code quality and testing: **led migration** from Enzyme to React Testing Library, set up Jest/SWC, and maintained GitLab CI visual-regression (WDIO) coverage.

work.name: Diesel Puppet
work.summary: **Built and owned the core technology** for Diesel Puppet, a casual HTML5 instant-games studio, across roughly five years. Designed and maintained a shared __TypeScript/PixiJS/Preact game engine__ (dp-instant) and its __NestJS/Firebase backend__, used to ship the same game codebase to ==seven-plus platforms== including Facebook Instant Games, VK, OK.ru, Yandex Games, GameDistribution and YouTube Playables.
highlights: **Built several titles end to end** on that platform: a 3D physics puzzle game (Babylon.js/cannon.js), a block-fit puzzle game, an asynchronous multiplayer word game that shipped ==45-plus versioned releases== over a year of near-daily development, a hidden-object puzzle game, and the core simulation engine for a territory-conquest strategy game built with an __entity-component-system architecture__.

Built the backend systems behind these games: a Firebase-backed Messenger bot service, and its successor, a __multi-tenant NestJS backend__ serving ==eight-plus titles== with shared auth, scoring, leaderboards, in-game payments and an asynchronous challenge/matchmaking system.
Set up and iterated on the studio's __CI/CD release pipeline__, including a migration from Bitbucket Pipelines to GitHub Actions.

work.name: FRVR
work.summary: **Built gameplay features and live-ops systems** in JavaScript on __a custom PixiJS-based engine__, with deep Facebook Instant Games SDK integration (cloud saves, leaderboards, social contexts, rewarded video).
highlights: **Owned the long-term goals and progression system** for Basketball FRVR end-to-end — data model, animated UI, reward economy and cross-session cloud sync — shipped behind A/B tests.
**Drove engine 2.0 migration**, low-end device performance work and ad-monetization integrations (LifeStreet, AdMob, Facebook Audience Network).
Ran ==436 releases of 10 titles== across web and Facebook Instant, localized into ==29 languages==.
